# Distributed MoE Inference (ggml-rpc)

Multi-node distributed inference for Qwen3.5-122B-A10B Q4_K_M across 4-5 NVIDIA GPU nodes.

**Trigger conditions (load this skill when):**
- User asks about 122B distributed inference (performance, config, benchmarks, startup params)
- User asks about Qwen 122B MoE model serving, RPC cluster, or GPU allocation
- User mentions "122B" or "Qwen3.5-122B" in context of multi-node inference
- User is searching for 122B benchmark/tok/s records — this skill IS the authoritative source
- User wants to start/stop/troubleshoot the 4-node RPC cluster (.17/.22/.28/.21)

**Documentation location**: Production 122B performance records (33.5 tok/s, full config,
GPU distribution) live HERE in this skill and its `references/`. The codebase `docs/` and
`tools/andl-docs/` directories contain only historical/partial benchmarks (pipeline mode,
35B model, heterogeneous deployments) — NOT the current production RPC config.

**Benchmark report**: The authoritative 4-node 122B benchmark with exact launch parameters is at
`~/.hermes/reports/qwen122b-4node-benchmark-20260613.md` (report) and
`~/.hermes/reports/qwen122b-4node-benchmark-20260613.json` (raw data). Always consult
this before starting the cluster — it contains the verified command that achieved 33.5 tok/s.

## Model Capabilities

Qwen3.5-122B-A10B is a **text-only model in llama.cpp's current implementation**, but the upstream model is a **Unified Vision-Language Foundation** with native multimodal support via early fusion. See `references/qwen35-multimodal-capability.md` for full details.

### `-sm layer` with `build/bin/` (June 11) — WORKS at 28.4 tok/s

**`-sm layer` IS viable with the `build/bin/` binary (June 11, full ARCH set: 500-1200).** Tested 2026-06-19 on 4×16GB GPUs:

```
build/bin/ -sm layer -ngl 99 -fit off --parallel 1 --no-warmup
→ 28.4 tok/s gen, 32.9 tok/s PP, 500ms TTFT
```

This is **33% faster** than the pre-UVM layer-split peak (21.3 tok/s from June 10), thanks to Blackwell-optimized CUDA kernels in `build/bin/` (ARCHS includes 1200). The tensor distribution is balanced (83-97% VRAM across all 4 GPUs).

**Contrast with `build-rebased/` `-sm layer`**: The rebased binary also loads with `-sm layer` but performance is untested (loading was interrupted). The rebased binary has different RPC and memory allocation behavior — the June 11 `build/bin/` is the known-good binary for layer-split.

**Why it works when older tests failed**: Earlier tests (June 10-12) used `build-rpc/` or `build-znver5/` binaries that lacked Blackwell arch support or had RPC allocation bugs. The `build/bin/` from June 11 was compiled with full architecture support (ARCHS=500,...,1200) and the correct RPC backend version. **Worker binary consistency is critical** — all workers must use the identical `build/bin/` binaries from the master, or tensor distribution breaks with 25+ GB allocations on 16 GB GPUs.

## 4-Node Setup (Stable)

## ANDL Pipeline (Alternative to RPC — cross-machine layer sharding)

The ANDL Pipeline (`pipeline-node-a`/`pipeline-node-b`) splits model layers across machines using gRPC streaming. Node A processes layers `[0, mid)` and sends hidden states to Node B, which processes layers `[mid, n_layer)` and returns logits. This is a fundamentally different architecture from `--split-mode row --rpc` — it splits **compute** (not just storage) across GPUs.

**When RPC `-sm row` is storage-only (rebased code without pipeline patches), the ANDL Pipeline is the ONLY way to achieve multi-node compute distribution.**

### Build & Deploy

```bash
# Build (direct g++ — NOT cmake):
cd /home/jialine/code/llama.cpp/tools/andl-pipeline
LLAMA_DIR="/home/jialine/code/llama.cpp"
BIN_DIR="/home/jialine/code/llama.cpp/build-rebased/bin"
BUILD_DIR="$BIN_DIR/.."
INC="-I$LLAMA_DIR -I$LLAMA_DIR/common -I$LLAMA_DIR/ggml/include -I$LLAMA_DIR/include -I$LLAMA_DIR/src -I$BUILD_DIR/common -I."
LIBS="-L$BIN_DIR -lllama -lllama-common -lggml -lggml-cpu -lggml-base"
RPATH="-Wl,-rpath,$BIN_DIR"
GRPC_FLAGS="$(pkg-config --cflags --libs grpc++ protobuf 2>/dev/null || echo '')"
STD="-std=c++17 -O2 -mavx2 -mfma"

g++ $STD $INC node_b.cpp pipeline.pb.cc pipeline.grpc.pb.cc $LIBS $RPATH $GRPC_FLAGS -lpthread -ldl -lm -o "$BIN_DIR/pipeline-node-b"
g++ $STD $INC node_a.cpp pipeline.pb.cc pipeline.grpc.pb.cc $LIBS $RPATH $GRPC_FLAGS -lpthread -ldl -lm -o "$BIN_DIR/pipeline-node-a"

# Deploy to workers:
tar czhf /tmp/pipeline-worker.tar.gz pipeline-node-b libllama.so libggml*.so libllama-common.so
scp /tmp/pipeline-worker.tar.gz jialine@192.168.0.17:/tmp/
ssh jialine@192.168.0.17 "cd ~/pipeline && tar xzf /tmp/pipeline-worker.tar.gz"
```

### Run (35B model, 40 layers, split at 20)

```bash
# === Node B (worker, layers 20-39) ===
ssh jialine@192.168.0.17 "cd ~/pipeline && \
  LLAMA_MOE_TOPK_PER_LAYER=4 LLAMA_N_GPU_LAYERS=20 \
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH=. ./pipeline-node-b Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf 20 50051"

# === Node A (master, layers 0-19) ===
cd /home/jialine/code/llama.cpp/build-rebased/bin
LLAMA_MOE_TOPK_PER_LAYER=4 LLAMA_N_GPU_LAYERS=20 LD_LIBRARY_PATH=. \
  ./pipeline-node-a /home/jialine/models/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-UD-Q4_K_XL.gguf 20 \
  192.168.0.17:50051 "What is the capital of France?"
```

### ⛔ CRITICAL: n_gpu_layers offset when n_layer_start > 0

`n_gpu_layers` counts from the END of ALL layers (`n_layer_all`), NOT from `n_layer_start`. When Node B loads only layers 20-39 with `n_layer_start=20`:
- `n_gpu_layers=999` → tries to put ALL 40 layers on GPU → OOM (20.8GB > 16GB)
- `n_gpu_layers=20` → `i_gpu_start = 41-20 = 21` → layers 21-39 on GPU, layer 20 on CPU
- `n_gpu_layers=21` → `i_gpu_start = 41-21 = 20` → layers 20-39 ALL on GPU (~10.9GB, fits 16GB)

**Rule**: for Node B, set `LLAMA_N_GPU_LAYERS = n_layer_all - n_layer_start + 1` (= 41 - start_layer) to put all loaded layers on GPU.

### ⛔ CRITICAL: qwen35moe.cpp output_norm double-application bug

**Bug**: When `partial_end_layer > 0`, the model graph still applied `output_norm` + `lm_head` on EVERY pipeline node. Node A (non-final) normalized its output, sending corrupted hidden states to Node B. Node B then normalized again, producing garbled output.

**Fix** (in `src/models/qwen35moe.cpp`): Gate output_norm + lm_head behind `is_final_node`:
```cpp
const bool is_final_node = (hparams.partial_end_layer == 0 ||
                            hparams.partial_end_layer >= n_layer);
if (is_final_node) {
    // output_norm → lm_head → logits
} else {
    // expose raw hidden state for next pipeline stage
    res->t_embd = cur;
}
```

**Symptom before fix**: Output was garbled Chinese/German/unicode mix instead of coherent English. **After fix**: correct output ("The capital of France is **Paris**.") confirmed 2026-06-18.

### Pipeline Performance (35B, RTX 5080 + RTX 4070 Ti)

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Node A decode (5080, 20 layers) | 27.5ms → 36 tok/s |
| Node B decode (4070 Ti, 20 layers) | ~45ms → 22 tok/s |
| Per-token roundtrip (incl. gRPC) | ~58ms → 17 tok/s |
| Generation-only | ~16 tok/s |
| Bottleneck | Worker GPU (4070 Ti slower than 5080) |

To reach 30+ tok/s: faster worker GPU, asymmetric split (master gets more layers), or pipeline overlap (process token N+1 on A while B processes token N).

### Option B: -ngl 99 with --split-mode row, UVM on master only (HISTORICAL — 33.5 tok/s with ANDL pipeline)

This was the production configuration BEFORE the rebase. It REQUIRES the ANDL Pipeline code that is now missing. Workers use pure VRAM (no UVM). Master uses UVM capped at 44 GB.

```bash
# === Workers (.22, .17, .28): Pure VRAM, NO UVM ===
cd /home/jialine/code/llama.cpp
./build/bin/rpc-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 50052

# === Master (.21): UVM capped at 44 GB ===
cd /home/jialine/code/llama.cpp
export GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1
export GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB=44
export LLAMA_MOE_TOPK_PER_LAYER=0-47:4

./build/bin/llama-server \
  --model /home/jialine/models/qwen3.5-122b-q4km/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  --rpc 192.168.0.22:50052,192.168.0.17:50052,192.168.0.28:50052 \
  -ngl 99 --split-mode row \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --no-webui --reasoning off
```

## Performance

### Current Production (moe-split `0caeec6b1`, tagged `stable-distributed-122b-topk4`, 2026-06-21)

122B Q4_K_M + topk=4 pruning (41% speedup vs default topk=8), UVM=44GB mast
er, 256K ctx q8_0 KV, `-b 4096 -ub 768`.

| Benchmark | Prompt tokens | Gen tok/s | PP tok/s | Notes |
|-----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|------|
| Short prompt | 16 | ~23 tok/s | — | Single micro-batch, RPC latency dominated |
| Long prompt | 205 | **~30 tok/s** | ~400-489 tok/s | PP scales with batch (long prompts amortize RPC overhead) |
| 1000-token gen | 52 | **29.9 tok/s** | — | Sustained, no degradation over time |
| Short PP | 144 | — | ~62 tok/s | Single micro-batch, RPC delay dominates |
| Long PP | 1400 | — | ~489 tok/s | Amortized pipeline |

- **⛔ RPC backend does NOT support GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_2 (expert-axis splitting)**: Changing MoE expert tensors in `llama-model.cpp` from `SPLIT_AXIS_1` (FFN dimension → tensor parallelism) to `SPLIT_AXIS_2` (expert dimension → expert parallelism) causes silent deadlock during RPC model loading. The model info prints then the process hangs — no error, no crash. The RPC split buffer logic only handles AXIS_0 and AXIS_1. For intra-layer MoE parallelism via expert distribution, either fix `ggml-rpc.cpp` split logic first, or use the scheduler-only approach (keep AXIS_1, parallelize MUL_MAT_ID across backends using tensor parallelism). See `references/moe-parallel-ax2-failure-20260621.md`.
- **`-b 4096 -ub 768` is the stable ceiling**: `-ub 1024` OOMs on .22 even with q4_0 KV. Do NOT attempt larger batch sizes — user directive.

### MoE Parallelization (2026-06-21/22)

Full design: `references/moe-parallelization-design-20260621.md`. Architecture diagram: `/home/jialine/code/llama.cpp/.hermes/moe-parallel-architecture.html`.

**Path C — Parallel Split Dispatch IMPLEMENTED (2026-06-22)**:
`GGML_SCHED_PARALLEL_SPLITS=1` enables concurrent dispatch of independent splits (different backends) via `std::thread` in `ggml_backend_sched_compute_splits`. MoE cache operations are mutex-protected. See `references/moe-parallelization-design-20260621.md#path-c-parallel-split-dispatch--implemented-2026-06-22` for implementation details, thread-safety design, and the `calloc`+`std::mutex` workaround.

**⛔ Path C BLOCKED: RPC client NOT thread-safe (2026-06-22)**: Parallel dispatch deadlocks on RPC backends — `std::thread::join()` blocks forever at `ggml_backend_graph_compute_async` → RPC socket. Multiple threads share RPC client state. Stack trace: `pthread_join ← ggml_backend_sched_compute_splits ← graph_compute ← llama_decode`. This is SEPARATE from the ///// correctness bug (which also exists when parallel execution is enabled). Fixing requires per-backend RPC connection pools (major refactor) or global mutex (serializes → zero gain). **Keep GGML_SCHED_PARALLEL_SPLITS=0 for RPC clusters.**

**Current limitation**: `-sm row` produces single-backend waves → no parallelism benefit. Path C becomes useful AFTER RPC supports AXIS_2 expert-axis splitting, enabling alternating-backend expert groups within a single layer.

**⛔ AXIS_2 expert splitting is BROKEN with RPC (2026-06-21)**: Changing MoE expert tensors from `GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_1` (FFN dimension) to `GGML_BACKEND_SPLIT_AXIS_2` (expert dimension) in `llama-model.cpp` causes a silent deadlock during RPC model loading. The process prints model info and stops — no error, no crash, just hangs forever. The RPC backend's split logic does not handle expert-axis partitioning of 3D MoE weight tensors. **Do NOT change split axis without also fixing RPC buffer/split logic in `ggml-rpc.cpp`.** See `references/moe-parallel-ax2-failure-20260621.md`.

## Server Flag Notes

- **`--jinja`**: Default ON for server. Controls chat template engine (full Jinja2 C++ engine vs legacy `llama_chat_apply_template` C API). Adding it explicitly is redundant but harmless. Not performance-relevant — only affects complex chat template compatibility (e.g., multi-tool templates that fail with `"try using --jinja"`).
- **`--mmproj` / `-mm`**: IRRELEVANT for Qwen3.5-122B. This flag specifies a separate vision-encoder GGUF for models like LLaVA/Qwen2.5-VL. Qwen3.5 uses early fusion (vision baked into weights), so no mmproj file exists or is needed. See `references/qwen35-multimodal-capability.md`.

## Key Constraints

- **-ngl 32 max** without UVM. -ngl 33 causes OOM on .19 (5060 Ti, 15.93 GiB usable).
- **-ngl 48 with UVM on master only** — see UVM section below. 5080 VRAM oversubscribes to 44.3 GB via system RAM.
- Blackwell GPUs (RTX 5060 Ti) REQUIRE Open Kernel Module driver.
- KV cache at 256K context: must use q8_0 (FP16 would be ~24 GB, q8_0 ~12 GB).
- AVX2 only (NO AVX-512 due to AMD bugs), target x86-64-v3.

### ⛔ CRITICAL: rpc-server MUST use --host 0.0.0.0

**The `rpc-server` binary defaults to binding `127.0.0.1` (localhost only).** Without `--host 0.0.0.0`, the master's `--rpc 192.168.0.x:50052` connections appear to succeed (TCP handshake via localhost) but actual tensor data never reaches the worker GPUs. Result: all 71GB of model weights stay on the master GPU → single-GPU bottleneck → ~8 tok/s instead of 29.5 tok/s.

**Symptoms of missing `--host 0.0.0.0`:**
- Worker GPU utilization: **0%** during inference (all workers idle)
- Worker VRAM: **~250 MB** (rpc-server process only, no model weights)
- Master GPU utilization: **100%** (alone doing all work)
- Master VRAM: **~15.8 GB** (full model + UVM overflow)
- `ss -tlnp | grep 50052` shows `127.0.0.1:50052` instead of `0.0.0.0:50052`
- Gen speed: ~8 tok/s (single-GPU-with-UVM, not distributed)

**Correct worker startup:**
```bash
./build/bin/rpc-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 50052
```

**What actually happens with --host 0.0.0.0 (the real RPC):** Each worker GPU receives its portion of the 71GB model (~12-15 GB each). During inference, all 4 GPUs participate: master at ~50% utilization, workers at ~6-13%. The 29.5 tok/s result is distributed inference, not single-GPU. See `references/gpu-profiling-20260613.md` for the before/after profiling data.

## UVM (Unified Memory) via CUDA

ggml-cuda.cu supports `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1` (no code changes needed for basic UVM).
This enables `cudaMallocManaged` — GPU can oversubscribe into system RAM.

### UMA Memory Limit (`GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB`) — CRITICAL for performance

Without a cap, ggml reads `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` to determine UMA memory size.
On a 96 GB system, this is ~62 GB free. The local GPU then "looks" like it has 62 GB available,
so ggml allocates most layers to it (45.3 GB), leaving workers underutilized at 7-9 GB each.

**The fix:** `GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB=44` caps the reported available memory for the local GPU.
With a 44 GB cap, ggml is forced to distribute layers more evenly across all GPUs.

This requires a **one-line code patch** to ggml-cuda.cu (see `references/uma-limit-patch.md`).
The patch adds `getenv("GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB")` support that caps `available_memory_kb` before
it's reported to the ggml allocator.

### Effect of UMA_LIMIT_GB

| UMA Limit | 5080 Buffer | Worker Buffers | Sys RAM Used | Gen tok/s |
|-----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| None (62 GB) | 45.3 GB | 7.5-9.0 GB | ~42 GB | 15.7 |
| 48 GB | 34.9 GB | 11.9 GB each | ~42 GB | 21.3 |
| **44 GB** | **35.0 GB** | **11.9 GB each** | **~20 GB** | **33.5** |

44 GB is the current optimum — matches or exceeds 48 GB in gen speed while saving ~22 GB system RAM (vs 42 GB at 48 GB).
The cap reduces the 5080's UVM overflow from 28.8 GB → 18.9 GB, pushing ~10.4 GB of
model weights to the 3 workers (each gaining 3-4 GB). Workers go from 46-55% → 82-86% VRAM
utilization. The result is a **55% speedup** over the default -ngl 32 config.

**Critical finding**: Remote RPC startup time scales non-linearly with `-ngl` for ALL quantization formats (Q4_K_M and IQ4_XS). This is NOT a deadlock — the process is compiling MoE compute graphs distributed across RPC nodes. Can take 10-15+ minutes for high GPU layer counts.

| IQ4_XS | 43-44 | 43-44 | **10-15+ min** | Full graph + ~55 GB transfer |

**Why so slow?** Each MoE layer with 256 experts creates a subgraph of operations distributed across 4 GPUs. With 44 GPU layers: ~792 tensors transferred over 1 Gbps (~125 MB/s shared across 3 workers). Plus CUDA graph capture for the full compute graph. Both scale super-linearly with layer count. Q4_K_M has larger tensors per layer but fewer layers offloaded at same -ngl.

**Symptoms**: 
- Port 8080 binds early (check: `ss -tlnp | grep 8080`) but health returns 503 for minutes
- Tensor loading dots complete quickly, then process appears frozen
- RSS stable, CPU at 10-15% → it's working, not dead
- File output is **block-buffered** — can't see progress in redirected logs

**Diagnostic trick — local RPC** to isolate network vs graph issues:
```bash

# Test with local RPC only

## Debugging Garbage Output: Binary Search on Commits

When the model produces garbled output (e.g., all `/////` characters, gibberish multilingual tokens, or scattered Chinese mixed with Latin/Arabic scripts), use **commit binary search** to find the regression point — it's the fastest way to isolate bugs in distributed RPC inference.

### Binary Search Procedure

1. **Start from a known-working commit** (for moe-split: `a7599826e` — pre-CUDA-kernel-replacement, generated text output on 2026-06-21)
2. **Build clean from scratch** each step: `rm -rf build && mkdir build && cmake .. && cmake --build .` — stale object files can mask the regression
3. **Check RPC proto version**: older commits may have a different `GGML_OP_COUNT` → `static_assert` failure in `ggml-rpc.h`. Fix by updating the count in the assertion.
4. **Deploy fresh rpc-server to all workers**: scp the rebuilt binary, kill old processes first (they lock the binary with "Text file busy")
5. **Test with a deterministic prompt** at low temperature (temp=0), checking for text vs garbage pattern
6. **Binary search**: test the midpoint commit between known-good and known-bad, narrow down

### CPU Layer Tradeoff (-ngl 46/47)

Reducing `-ngl` from 48 to 46-47 trades explicit CPU processing for reduced UVM overflow:

```
-ngl 48: 5080 34.9 GB → 18.9 GB UVM overflow → random page faults
-ngl 47: 5080 ~32 GB  → 16 GB UVM overflow   → 2 layers on CPU
-ngl 46: 5080 ~29 GB  → 13 GB UVM overflow   → 3 layers on CPU
```

CPU processes Q4_K_M layers at ~1.5-2ms/layer (predictable). UVM page faults are ~1-2ms each (unpredictable, stall GPU). The sweet spot is where CPU cost < UVM overhead saved. Not yet tested — theory only.

When rpc-server is killed (SIGKILL/-9) during an active RPC session, CUDA contexts on worker GPUs are NOT cleaned up. The GPU memory (12-16 GB) remains allocated to the zombie CUDA context. New rpc-server instances start but have only the remaining free VRAM, which may be insufficient for model tensor allocation.

**Symptoms:**
- `nvidia-smi` shows 11-12 GB used even though no rpc-server process is running
- Master fails with `failed to allocate RPC[X] buffer of size N` where N > free VRAM

- **256K KV cache initialization takes 20-25 minutes**: On first request after model load, the server creates 32 KV cache checkpoints (~149 MiB each) for the 256K context. The ANDL Pipeline (`pipeline-node-a`/`pipeline-node-b`) splits model layers across machines using gRPC streaming. if (is_final_node) {
    // output_norm → lm_head → logits
} else {
    // expose raw hidden state for next pipeline stage
    res->t_embd = cur;
}
```

- Master GPU utilization: **100%** (alone doing all work)

- `ss -tlnp | grep 50052` shows `127.0.0.1:50052` instead of `0.0.0.0:50052`
- Gen speed: ~8 tok/s (single-GPU-with-UVM, not distributed)

**Correct worker startup:**

**What actually happens with --host 0.0.0.0 (the real RPC):** Each worker GPU receives its portion of the 71GB model (~12-15 GB each). During inference, all 4 GPUs participate: master at ~50% utilization, workers at ~6-13%. The 29.5 tok/s result is distributed inference, not single-GPU. ## UVM (Unified Memory) via CUDA

ggml-cuda.cu supports `GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1` (no code changes needed for basic UVM).
This enables `cudaMallocManaged` — GPU can oversubscribe into system RAM.

### UMA Memory Limit (`GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB`) — CRITICAL for performance

Without a cap, ggml reads `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo` to determine UMA memory size.
On a 96 GB system, this is ~62 GB free. The local GPU then "looks" like it has 62 GB available,
so ggml allocates most layers to it (45.3 GB), leaving workers underutilized at 7-9 GB each.

**The fix:** `GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB=44` caps the reported available memory for the local GPU.
With a 44 GB cap, ggml is forced to distribute layers more evenly across all GPUs.

This requires a **one-line code patch** to ggml-cuda.cu (see `references/uma-limit-patch.md`).
The patch adds `getenv("GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB")` support that caps `available_memory_kb` before
it's reported to the ggml allocator.

### Effect of UMA_LIMIT_GB

| UMA Limit | 5080 Buffer | Worker Buffers | Sys RAM Used | Gen tok/s |
|-----------|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|
| None (62 GB) | 45.3 GB | 7.5-9.0 GB | ~42 GB | 15.7 |
| 48 GB | 34.9 GB | 11.9 GB each | ~42 GB | 21.3 |
| **44 GB** | **35.0 GB** | **11.9 GB each** | **~20 GB** | **33.5** |

44 GB is the current optimum — matches or exceeds 48 GB in gen speed while saving ~22 GB system RAM (vs 42 GB at 48 GB).
The cap reduces the 5080's UVM overflow from 28.8 GB → 18.9 GB, pushing ~10.4 GB of
model weights to the 3 workers (each gaining 3-4 GB). Workers go from 46-55% → 82-86% VRAM
utilization. The result is a **55% speedup** over the default -ngl 32 config.

### Master-only UVM (MANDATORY — workers must NEVER use UVM)

**⛔ Workers with UVM destroy performance.** Tested: worker UVM → 5.8-13.8 tok/s (vs 33.5 without). Workers have no system RAM headroom for page faults; every UVM spill competes with network RPC and GPU compute. Simply never set UVM on workers.

```bash

./build/bin/rpc-server --host 0.0.0.0 --port 50052

# On master (.21) ONLY:

export GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY=1
export GGML_CUDA_UMA_LIMIT_GB=44  # Current optimum
export LLAMA_MOE_TOPK_PER_LAYER=0-47:4

./build/bin/llama-server \
  --model /home/jialine/models/qwen3.5-122b-q4km/Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-Q4_K_M.gguf \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8080 \
  --rpc 192.168.0.22:50052,192.168.0.17:50052,192.168.0.28:50052 \
  -ngl 99 --split-mode row \
  --parallel 1 \
  -c 262144 \
  --cache-type-k q8_0 --cache-type-v q8_0 \
  --flash-attn on \
  --no-webui --reasoning off
```

**Why master-only UVM works and worker UVM fails:** The 5080 holds ~35 GB of model weights with 16 GB VRAM → ~19 GB UVM overflow. UVM page faults on the local PCIe bus (32 GB/s) are manageable. Workers each hold ~12 GB in their 16 GB VRAM → no overflow needed. When workers are forced into UVM, they report all 32 GB system RAM as available → ggml allocates 21+ GB per worker → massive page fault overhead across 1-2.5 Gbps network → catastrophic speed drop. **The rule: UVM on master, pure VRAM on workers.**

### RPC Startup Latency (Graph Compilation + Network) — Affects ALL Quantizations

**Critical finding**: Remote RPC startup time scales non-linearly with `-ngl` for ALL quantization formats (Q4_K_M and IQ4_XS). This is NOT a deadlock — the process is compiling MoE compute graphs distributed across RPC nodes. Can take 10-15+ minutes for high GPU layer counts.

| Model | -ngl | GPU layers | Startup time | Notes |
|-------|------|:---:|:---:|------|
| IQ4_XS | 4 | 4 | <10s | Tiny graph, instant |
| IQ4_XS | 20 | 20 | ~3-5 min | ~30 GB network transfer |
| Q4_K_M | 30 | 30 | ~3 min | Port listening at ~2 min, health 503 until ~3 min |
| Q4_K_M | 33 | 33 | ~3-5 min | Still 503 at 3 min |
| Q4_K_M | 36 | 36 | ~3-5 min | Confirmed loading: 36/49 layers, buffers 10.8/13.4/14.9/13.4 GB |
| IQ4_XS | 43-44 | 43-44 | **10-15+ min** | Full graph + ~55 GB transfer |

**Why so slow?** Each MoE layer with 256 experts creates a subgraph of operations distributed across 4 GPUs. With 44 GPU layers: ~792 tensors transferred over 1 Gbps (~125 MB/s shared across 3 workers). Plus CUDA graph capture for the full compute graph. Both scale super-linearly with layer count. Q4_K_M has larger tensors per layer but fewer layers offloaded at same -ngl.

**Symptoms**: 
- Port 8080 binds early (check: `ss -tlnp | grep 8080`) but health returns 503 for minutes
- Tensor loading dots complete quickly, then process appears frozen
- RSS stable, CPU at 10-15% → it's working, not dead
- File output is **block-buffered** — can't see progress in redirected logs

**Diagnostic trick — local RPC** to isolate network vs graph issues:
```bash
# Start local rpc-server on master
./build/bin/rpc-server -H 127.0.0.1 -p 50053 &
# Test with local RPC only
./build/bin/llama-server -m model.gguf -ngl 10 --rpc 127.0.0.1:50053 ...
# If this starts in seconds but remote RPC hangs → graph is fine, network is the bottleneck
```

**Mitigation**: Accept the long startup time — once loaded, inference speed is unaffected. For frequent restarts, prefer lower `-ngl` (e.g., 32-36 for Q4_K_M, 41 for IQ4_XS). Use `--no-warmup` to skip warmup inference. Plan for 10+ minute startup when pushing near GPU VRAM limits.

## Debugging Garbage Output: Binary Search on Commits

When the model produces garbled output (e.g., all `/////` characters, gibberish multilingual tokens, or scattered Chinese mixed with Latin/Arabic scripts), use **commit binary search** to find the regression point — it's the fastest way to isolate bugs in distributed RPC inference.

### Binary Search Procedure

1. **Start from a known-working commit** (for moe-split: `a7599826e` — pre-CUDA-kernel-replacement, generated text output on 2026-06-21)
2. **Build clean from scratch** each step: `rm -rf build && mkdir build && cmake .. && cmake --build .` — stale object files can mask the regression
3. **Check RPC proto version**: older commits may have a different `GGML_OP_COUNT` → `static_assert` failure in `ggml-rpc.h`. Fix by updating the count in the assertion.
4. **Deploy fresh rpc-server to all workers**: scp the rebuilt binary, kill old processes first (they lock the binary with "Text file busy")
5. **Test with a deterministic prompt** at low temperature (temp=0), checking for text vs garbage pattern
6. **Binary search**: test the midpoint commit between known-good and known-bad, narrow down

### CPU Layer Tradeoff (-ngl 46/47)

Reducing `-ngl` from 48 to 46-47 trades explicit CPU processing for reduced UVM overflow:

```
-ngl 48: 5080 34.9 GB → 18.9 GB UVM overflow → random page faults
-ngl 47: 5080 ~32 GB  → 16 GB UVM overflow   → 2 layers on CPU
-ngl 46: 5080 ~29 GB  → 13 GB UVM overflow   → 3 layers on CPU
```

CPU processes Q4_K_M layers at ~1.5-2ms/layer (predictable). UVM page faults are ~1-2ms each (unpredictable, stall GPU). The sweet spot is where CPU cost < UVM overhead saved. Not yet tested — theory only.

### ⛔ CRITICAL: Zombie GPU memory from killed rpc-server processes

When rpc-server is killed (SIGKILL/-9) during an active RPC session, CUDA contexts on worker GPUs are NOT cleaned up. The GPU memory (12-16 GB) remains allocated to the zombie CUDA context. New rpc-server instances start but have only the remaining free VRAM, which may be insufficient for model tensor allocation.

**Symptoms:**
- `nvidia-smi` shows 11-12 GB used even though no rpc-server process is running
- Master fails with `failed to allocate RPC[X] buffer of size N` where N > free VRAM
- Worker `ss -tlnp | grep 50052` shows rpc-server listening, but `nvidia-smi` shows high VRAM usage
- The log line `RPC1: 192.168.0.17:50052 (15943 MiB, 4236 MiB free)` — only 4 GB free on a 16 GB card

**Fix:** Physical reboot of the affected worker, or `sudo nvidia-smi -r` to reset the GPU. `pkill -9` does NOT free CUDA memory. A normal SIGTERM or clean shutdown (CTRL+C) is needed for proper cleanup. If SSH is unresponsive, the worker may need a hard power cycle.

**Prevention:** Always stop rpc-server with SIGTERM (`pkill rpc-server` without `-9`) or CTRL+C before restarting. Only use SIGKILL as last resort.

### ⛔ CRITICAL: Worker binary compilation — `GGML_NATIVE` pitfall

**`GGML_NATIVE=ON` (cmake default) appends `-march=native` to ggml-cpu compile flags, OVERRIDING any user-specified `-march=x86-64-v3`**. This happens in `ggml/src/ggml-cpu/CMakeLists.txt:306`. Result: binaries compiled on Ryzen 9700X (AVX-512) crash with `SIGILL` on Intel 13th/14th gen workers (no AVX-512).

**Fix:** Rebuild with `GGML_NATIVE=OFF` and explicitly enable needed features:
```bash
cmake .. \
  -DGGML_NATIVE=OFF \
  -DGGML_AVX2=ON \
  -DGGML_FMA=ON \
  -DGGML_F16C=ON \
  -DGGML_AVX=ON \
  -DGGML_AVX512=OFF
cmake --build . --target ggml-cpu rpc-server -j$(nproc)
```

**Verification:** `objdump -d build/bin/libggml-cpu.so.0 | grep -c zmm` must return 0 (zero AVX-512 instructions). Then re-enable `GGML_NATIVE=ON` on the master for its AVX-512 benefit before rebuilding `llama-server`. Two separate builds: worker rpc-server without native, master llama-server with native.

The file appears frozen at 177 lines for minutes while the process is actually working. **Fix**: Run foreground with `timeout N ...` to see real-time progress, or use `stdbuf -oL` / `unbuffer`. Different orders yield different per-GPU buffer sizes (e.g., same node got 14.0 GB vs 15.3 GB depending on position). Every attention operation must fetch K/V from CPU RAM → 0.9 tok/s (vs 11.3 tok/s with KV on GPU). **Fix**: Never use `--no-kv-offload` at large contexts. Keep KV cache on GPU — the UVM oversubscription penalty (11.3 tok/s) is 12.5x faster than CPU KV cache. The GPU page faults from UVM are orders of magnitude cheaper than PCIe roundtrips for every attention head.
